ip_top_stories.title: China Issues Draft Regulations on AI Copyright Infringement
ip_top_stories.summary: China has released draft regulations addressing copyright infringement in the context of AI, marking a significant step toward formal legislative oversight of AI-generated content and training data practices. The move reflects growing international regulatory momentum on AI and intellectual property. The draft sets out liability frameworks that could affect both domestic and international AI developers operating in China.

ip_top_stories.title: Tech's AI Coding Boom On Collision Course With Copyright
ip_top_stories.summary: The rapid expansion of AI-powered coding tools is raising unresolved copyright questions about the provenance of training data and the ownership of AI-generated code outputs. Legal experts warn that the industry is moving faster than the legal frameworks designed to govern it. The piece examines how existing copyright doctrine may struggle to accommodate the scale of code generation now occurring.

ip_top_stories.title: Delhi HC Examines Copyright Eligibility of AI-Generated Art in Landmark DABUS Case
ip_top_stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed India's Copyright Office to issue a ruling within eight weeks on Stephen Thaler's application for copyright protection of AI-generated artwork, in a case that directly tests whether AI-created works can receive copyright protection under Indian law. The court's order follows Thaler's separate lawsuit against the Indian government over the copyright deadlock. The decision is expected to have significant implications for AI authorship rights in India.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Code Leak Exposes the Fault Lines of Copyright
ip_top_stories.summary: A leaked AI code incident has brought into sharp relief the unresolved copyright fault lines surrounding AI-generated and AI-assisted software. The story examines how the leak highlights the legal ambiguities around ownership, liability, and the boundaries of copyright protection for AI outputs.

ip_top_stories.title: AI And Human Authorship Requirement: Reflections From The US Position And Implications For Indian Copyright Law
ip_top_stories.summary: An analysis of how the US Copyright Office's position on human authorship requirements for AI-generated works is shaping the debate in India, where courts are actively grappling with similar questions. The piece examines the doctrinal tensions between established copyright frameworks and the realities of AI-generated creative output. It draws on the ongoing Thaler litigation and broader comparative law to assess where Indian law may be headed.

ip_further_links.title: IP Rights in the Age of AI
ip_further_links.summary: A broad overview of how AI is reshaping intellectual property rights frameworks across multiple domains, including copyright, patents, and trade secrets.

ip_further_links.title: Fordham 33 (Report 2): Top 5 Takeaways: Data Governance, Privacy, & Cybersecurity in an AI World
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat reports key takeaways from the Fordham IP Conference panel on data governance, privacy, and cybersecurity in the context of AI, highlighting emerging international consensus points and areas of ongoing disagreement.

ip_further_links.title: Fordham 33 (Report 1): Government Leader's Perspective on IP
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat covers government leaders' perspectives on intellectual property policy at the Fordham IP Conference, including discussion of AI's impact on existing IP frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: Fordham 33 (Report 3): Top 5 Takeaways: The Global Divide in Design Protection
ip_further_links.summary: IPKat reports on the global divide in design protection discussed at the Fordham IP Conference, with implications for how AI-generated designs may be treated across different jurisdictions.

ip_further_links.title: Class action alleges Apple secretly scraped and trained its AI on YouTube videos
ip_further_links.summary: A class action lawsuit alleges that Apple covertly scraped YouTube videos without authorisation to train its AI models, adding to the wave of litigation targeting major tech companies over training data practices.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — The SSP Annual Meeting: Keeping the Faith in Unsettled Times
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen previews the SSP Annual Meeting, examining how scholarly publishing organisations are navigating uncertainty around AI, intellectual property, and the evolving research communications landscape.
